title: Feedback balance simulator is orphaned: 8 files, 817 LOC, zero importers
body:
## Summary
The whole src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/ subtree (FeedbackBalanceSimulator and its 7 parts) is mounted nowhere; SimulatorTab renders only the predictive simulator.

## Description
FeedbackBalanceSimulator is the context map's declared "feedback-based simulator" entry point, but no file imports it (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/SimulatorTab.tsx:6 imports only PredictiveBalanceSimulator). The subtree still carries live defects that only matter if it is shown: formatMetricValue renders a 100% survival rate as "1.0%" because it only scales values < 1 (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/types.ts:59); DeltaBadge builds "var(--color-border)26" as a background, which is invalid CSS, so neutral badges lose their fill (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/FeedbackMetric.tsx:87); the run seeds from the wall clock (already a recorded encounter-balance-simulation deviation); the iterations input has no upper clamp (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/ConfigPanel.tsx:93). Whether to re-mount it (the declared capability) or delete it (and drop its motion-loop-guard allowlist row and context-map entry) is a product call.

## Flow
- Open Character > Simulator: only the matrix, the radar and the predictive simulator render
- grep for FeedbackBalanceSimulator outside feedback/: 0 hits
- Decide: re-mount (then fix the 3 defects above, test-first) or delete the subtree plus src/__tests__/a11y/motion-loop-guard.test.ts:100 and the context-map paths

## Expected impact
Either the designer regains the feel-vs-math comparison the context promises, or 817 LOC of unreachable code and its allowlist row leave the tree. Deleting removes a capability the context description names.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one declared capability is either reachable or gone
Before: 0 importers of FeedbackBalanceSimulator; 817 LOC unreachable; 3 latent defects
After: mounted with the 3 defects fixed, or 0 LOC
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep over src, e2e, docs, scripts
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep -rn FeedbackBalanceSimulator src e2e docs scripts (excluding feedback/): 0 importers
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/SimulatorTab.tsx:4-6 imports ComparisonMatrix, ArchetypeBalanceRadar, PredictiveBalanceSimulator only
find src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback -type f | xargs cat | wc -l -> 817
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/types.ts:59 if (value < 1 && unit === '%') -> survivalRate 1.0 renders "1.0%"
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/feedback/FeedbackMetric.tsx:87 `${neutral ? 'var(--color-border)' : color}${OPACITY_15}` -> "var(--color-border)26"

title: Radar heatmap legend hard-codes the 10%/25% thresholds deviationColor owns
body:
## Summary
The Stat Deviation Heatmap legend prints "<10%" and ">=25%" as literals while the colouring rule lives in sub_character/_shared/data.ts deviationColor.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/ArchetypeBalanceRadar.tsx:148 and :156 restate the thresholds that src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/_shared/data.ts:436-441 implements (abs < 0.1 success, < 0.25 warning). They agree today; change one and the legend lies. Fix: export DEVIATION_THRESHOLDS from _shared/data.ts, have deviationColor and the legend both read it, pinned by a test that renders the legend and asserts it states the exported values. _shared is owned by character-overview-input this wave, so out of scope here.

## Flow
- Export DEVIATION_THRESHOLDS = { balanced: 0.1, outlier: 0.25 } from _shared/data.ts
- deviationColor reads it; legend formats it
- Test: render ArchetypeBalanceRadar, assert legend text derives from the constant

## Expected impact
Designers reading the legend keep a correct key when thresholds are retuned. Could break nothing beyond the legend string.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one threshold source
Before: 2 sites (1 rule + 1 hand-copied legend)
After: 1 source, 2 readers
Method: simulation - walked a retune of 0.1 to 0.15: legend would still print <10%; _shared is sibling-owned this wave
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test asserting the legend text equals the exported thresholds, seeded red by changing the constant

title: Radar score-delta colour is hue-only with unexplained 3%/8% thresholds
body:
## Summary
Each composite-score badge colours its delta green/amber/red by inline magic thresholds with no legend and no non-colour cue.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/ArchetypeBalanceRadar.tsx:58-59 picks STATUS_SUCCESS/WARNING/ERROR at |delta| < 0.03 / < 0.08 and paints only the text colour (:82). Nothing on screen says what the colours mean, and a colour-blind reader gets no signal (WCAG 1.4.1). The repo's StatusToken/StatusTag (colour + glyph) is the shared answer. Fix: name the thresholds, render the band via StatusTag or add a glyph and an aria/visible band word, plus a legend line.

## Flow
- Render the radar with 4 characters
- Delta "(+5.2)" is amber with no explanation and no glyph
- Fix: band word/glyph + legend line, constants named

## Expected impact
Balance outliers become readable without colour. Low risk: presentation only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - outlier band legible without hue
Before: 0 of 3 bands carry a non-colour cue; 0 legend lines
After: 3 of 3; 1 legend line
Method: simulation - read the render path; no test exists for the badge
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/ArchetypeBalanceRadar.tsx:58-59 const deltaColor = Math.abs(delta) < 0.03 ? STATUS_SUCCESS : Math.abs(delta) < 0.08 ? STATUS_WARNING : STATUS_ERROR;
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/ArchetypeBalanceRadar.tsx:82 style={{ color: deltaColor }}
instrument: component test: badge for a +0.09 delta exposes the band word/glyph (red before, green after)

title: Character comparison has no empty state when the selection is cleared
body:
## Summary
Clearing the ScalableSelector leaves a stat-only table, an empty radar and an empty heatmap with no prompt to add characters.

## Description
ScalableSelector exposes a clear action (src/components/shared/ScalableSelector/index.tsx:156 onSelect([])), so comparisonIds can be []. ComparisonMatrix then renders six stat rows with no columns (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/ComparisonMatrix.tsx:88,97), ArchetypeBalanceRadar renders RadarChart with data [] (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/ArchetypeBalanceRadar.tsx:167-170) and a heatmap with headers only; with one character, every deviation is 0 and the radar has nothing to compare. Fix: an explicit empty/one-character state in both panels ("Pick at least two characters to compare").

## Flow
- Simulator > Character Comparison > Add > clear
- Matrix shows labels only; radar draws an empty polygon
- Fix: empty state below 2 selections

## Expected impact
A designer is told what to do instead of reading blank panels. No data path changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the empty selection is a designed state
Before: 0 of 2 panels render an empty/one-character state
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - traced the clear path; component tests would need the selector open
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render ComparisonMatrix with selected=[] and ArchetypeBalanceRadar with balanceResults=[]; assert an empty-state message

title: Encounter edits build the next array from render-time config, not the updater
body:
## Summary
ConfigPanel encounter archetype/count onChange copy config.enemyConfigs from the render closure and then pass it into a functional setConfig updater.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/predictive/ConfigPanel.tsx:131-133 and :149-151 do const next = [...config.enemyConfigs]; ...; setConfig(c => ({ ...c, enemyConfigs: next })). The updater ignores c.enemyConfigs, so two edits batched before a re-render (or an edit racing applyTuning/undo, which also setConfig) drop the earlier one. Fix: build next from c inside the updater.

## Flow
- Two enemy-config edits dispatched in one React batch
- The second updater overwrites with an array copied from the pre-batch render
- First edit lost

## Expected impact
Edits never silently revert. Risk: none beyond these two handlers.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no lost encounter edit under batching
Before: 2 handlers read the closure
After: 0
Method: simulation - walked a batched double-dispatch; not reproduced in the UI
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test calling both onChange handlers inside act() before re-render, asserting both edits survive

title: DPS breakdown is labelled per encounter but never depends on the encounter
body:
## Summary
The engine computes one identical static per-ability DPS list for every encounter label, and the chart titles it with the first encounter.

## Description
src/lib/combat/predictive-balance.ts:551-559 builds dpsBreakdowns[label] from midAttrs and PLAYER_ABILITIES only (no archetype, no fight), so every encounter's entry is the same array. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/predictive/DPSBreakdownChart.tsx:12,18 shows entries[0] titled "<encounter> - Effective DPS/ability", implying an encounter-specific number. Fix: the engine emits one breakdown keyed by mid level, the chart titles it "Lv.<mid> player - static DPS per ability". The engine file is outside this context.

## Flow
- Run a sweep with 4 encounters
- Compare report.dpsBreakdowns values across labels: identical
- Chart title names one encounter

## Expected impact
Designers stop reading a static ability table as an encounter outcome. Risk: report shape change has in-tree consumers to update.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the chart says what the number is
Before: 4 identical arrays under 4 encounter keys; title names an encounter
After: 1 array; title names the player level
Method: simulation - read the engine loop; a probe over runPredictiveBalance would assert equality
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test: runPredictiveBalance with 2 encounters -> dpsBreakdowns values deep-equal (red after the reshape is the guard)

title: Cell tuner target clamps per keystroke, so a cleared field becomes 0
body:
## Summary
CellTuner reconciles the target-survival input on every change, turning an emptied field into 0 mid-edit.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/simulator/predictive/CellTuner.tsx:126 setTargetPct(Math.min(100, Math.max(0, +e.target.value))). Clearing "80" to retype yields "" -> 0 shown immediately; the stepper contract (software-engineering ui-controls micro-interaction-contracts, The stepper) says reconcile at commit (blur/Solve), and the empty field is a state, not a zero. Fix: hold a string draft, clamp on blur and at Solve.

## Flow
- Select a heatmap cell
- Select-all + Backspace in Target %
- Field shows 0

## Expected impact
Retyping a target stops fighting the keyboard. Risk: Solve must clamp the draft.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - typed input reconciled at commit
Before: empty field -> 0 on 1 keystroke
After: empty stays empty until blur/Solve
Method: simulation - read the handler
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: test: change target to "" -> input value stays "" ; blur -> clamps
